claims.statement: The pnpm workspace is exactly two globs, `apps/*` and `packages/*`, which yield six members (admin, mobile, server, @komyuter/shared, @repo/ui, @repo/typescript-config) and deliberately exclude `navbench/`, so the benchmark harness's Rust, Go and Node toolchains are never touched by `pnpm install` or a Turbo graph.

The package manager is pinned to pnpm 8 by `"packageManager": "pnpm@8.15.6"` in the root package.json (authoritative over stale docs claiming pnpm 9+/10.12+), the lockfile is in pnpm-8 format (`lockfileVersion: '6.0'`), and CI installs that same version because `pnpm/action-setup@v4` is configured with no `version` input and therefore reads the `packageManager` field.

Root `.npmrc` enables `auto-install-peers = true`, while `apps/mobile/.npmrc` is the only per-package override and switches that member to `node-linker=hoisted` and turns on pre/post lifecycle scripts.

The root package.json is the sole gate entrypoint set: `build`/`dev`/`test` delegate to `turbo run <task>`, `lint` is a bare repo-wide `eslint .` (not a Turbo task), `typecheck` is a hard-coded chain of five `tsc --noEmit` invocations (four by `-p <tsconfig>` plus `pnpm --filter mobile typecheck`), `format`/`format:check` run Prettier over `**/*.{ts,tsx,md}`, and `prepare` installs husky.

`turbo.json` declares four tasks — `build` (dependsOn `^build`, inputs `$TURBO_DEFAULT$` plus `.env*`, outputs `dist/**`), `test` (inputs `$TURBO_DEFAULT$` plus `.env*`), `lint` (`{}`) and `dev` (`cache: false`, `persistent: true`) — and declares no `typecheck` task, so the typecheck gate runs entirely outside Turbo and gets no Turbo caching or filtering.

Only `apps/admin` (`tsc && vite build`) and `apps/server` (`tsc`) define a `build` script, so `turbo run build` never builds `@komyuter/shared` or `@repo/ui` — both ship TypeScript source through their `exports` maps (`./src/index.ts`, `./index.ts`) and rely on the consuming toolchain to resolve it — and `apps/mobile` declares no build script at all.

Only `apps/admin` and `apps/server` define a `test` script (`vitest run` each), so `pnpm test` (`turbo run test`) spans both suites; `apps/mobile` defines neither `test` nor `build` and therefore participates in the pipeline only through its `dev`, `lint` and `typecheck` scripts.

The `lint` task declared in `turbo.json` has no caller: no root script invokes `turbo run lint`, and `apps/mobile` is the only package that still declares a package-level `lint` script (`eslint .`), which is already redundant with the root repo-wide `eslint .` that covers mobile through the flat config's scoping blocks.

Linting is one root ESLint 9 flat config whose shape is: a global ignore list (`node_modules`, `dist`, `.turbo`, `public`, `apps/mobile/.expo`, `navbench/**`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`), three file sets (`webUiFiles`, `mobileFiles`, `serverFiles`), Expo's shared configs re-prefixed into `apps/mobile` by the `scopeExpo` helper, `@eslint/js` + non-type-aware `typescript-eslint` recommended rules scoped to web-UI and server files, react-hooks/react-refresh rules plus browser globals for web UI files, node globals for config files and server files, and `eslint-config-prettier` last to disable formatting rules.

The flat config still contains globs for `apps/web`, an app that no longer exists, and the removed `@repo/eslint-config` package / `.eslintrc.*` files must not be recreated; the root README.md still describes the create-turbo starter with a `web` app and `@repo/eslint-config`.

Prettier is configured with semicolons, double quotes, LF line endings and the Tailwind class-sorting plugin (with `cva` as a recognized function); because the root `format`/`format:check` globs cover only `.ts`, `.tsx` and `.md`, JSON, CSS and YAML formatting is enforced only by lint-staged, on staged files, locally.

`.prettierignore` excludes `node_modules`, `dist`, `.turbo`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `supabase/.temp`, the five root design docs and the entire `/openwiki` directory (with a documented rationale: generated wiki output plus the hand-authored INSTRUCTIONS.md would otherwise fail both `format:check` and lint-staged), but it does not exclude `navbench` — so navbench Markdown remains inside the format gate while `navbench/**` JavaScript is ESLint-ignored and outside every Turbo task.

Husky is installed through the root `prepare` script; `.husky/pre-commit` performs a warn-only branch-name allowlist check (`main`/`master`/`develop` or one of eleven `{type}/` prefixes, never failing the commit) and then runs `pnpm lint-staged`, while `.husky/commit-msg` is a one-line `pnpm commitlint --edit "$1"`.

lint-staged runs `pnpm exec eslint` on staged `.ts`/`.tsx` and `pnpm exec prettier --check` on staged `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.json`/`.md`, with no `--fix` or `--write`, so a lint error or formatting drift blocks the commit and must be repaired manually rather than being auto-corrected.

Commitlint extends `@commitlint/config-conventional` and adds a `scope-enum` rule listing eleven scopes (`web`, `ui`, `mobile`, `admin`, `server`, `shared`, `db`, `docs`, `config`, `ci`, `deps`) at severity 1, i.e. warn, so only the `type(scope): description` shape is actually enforced and an unknown scope merely produces a warning.

CI is a single non-matrix job named `check` on `ubuntu-latest` triggered by every `push` and every `pull_request`, running sequentially: checkout, `pnpm/action-setup`, `actions/setup-node` (Node 20 with the pnpm store cache), `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm --filter admin test` and `pnpm build`, so the first failing step stops the rest and a red format check never reaches the build.

The CI test step deliberately uses `pnpm --filter admin test` instead of `pnpm test`/`turbo run test` because the server suite's integration half needs a live Supabase stack; the repo constitution makes `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm format:check` and the admin suite mandatory pre-merge gates enforced by CI, and `pnpm --filter server test` mandatory only whenever a change touches `apps/server` or `packages/shared`, which is therefore a real gate no automation enforces.

The admin suite is the only behavioural gate in CI: hermetic, node-environment, limited to `src/tests/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}` (23 files / 311 tests per AGENTS.md), with `passWithNoTests: true` in its Vitest config — which means a broken include pattern or emptied test directory makes the step pass with zero tests executed.

The server suite cannot be a hermetic CI step on its own terms: its Vitest config disables file parallelism because the integration files share one real Postgres database, snapshots and restores that database through a `globalSetup`, and allows 30-second timeouts.

`pnpm typecheck` covers five TypeScript projects (packages/ui, apps/admin, apps/mobile through its own script, apps/server, packages/shared) under `strict: true` inherited from `@repo/typescript-config/base.json`, but no project's `include` list covers repo-level configuration files — `apps/admin/tsconfig.json` includes only `src`, and `apps/server/tsconfig.json` includes only `src` and `tests` — so `vite.config.ts`, `vitest.config.ts`, `drizzle.config.ts` and `eslint.config.mjs` are linted but never type-checked.
The only caching in CI is the pnpm store (via `actions/setup-node` with `cache: pnpm`); the workflow has no Turbo remote cache, no artifacts/reports, no matrix job and no branch filter.

The repository's only other automation is `.github/workflows/openwiki-update.yml`: `workflow_dispatch` plus a daily cron, Node 22, npm-installed `openwiki@0.7.1` (with mermaid/jsdom), `openwiki code --update`, removal of `openwiki/.run.json`, and a `docs: update OpenWiki` pull request on branch `openwiki/update` restricted to `openwiki`, `AGENTS.md`, the workflow file and `CLAUDE.md` when present — it is a docs refresh, not a quality gate.

Documented build/CI claims disagree with the config in three places: `docs/TECHSTACK.md` sketches a CI running typecheck/lint/test/`migration-lint` on pull requests to main/develop while the workflow has no `migration-lint`, no test step and no branch filter; specs and `docs/ADMIN.md` cite `pnpm --filter admin lint`, a script that no longer exists anywhere except as the mobile package's own `lint`; and `apps/server/README.md` requires Node 22 LTS while CI pins Node 20.
